scenes.title: Amazon Lex
scenes.narration: Amazon Lex builds conversational interfaces around user intentions and required parameters. If a customer says I want to reserve a meeting room, the intent describes the task; slots capture information such as date, location and room size. The bot requests missing values, validates them, and can call a configured fulfillment function such as AWS Lambda. An actual booking must not be committed until the application checks availability and authorization, and any necessary confirmation is received. Lex is different from Polly and Transcribe because it manages the dialogue logic rather than only converting between text and audio. Some older integrations may mention Amazon Kendra for knowledge search, but that is a historical or existing-customer option. For a new retrieval architecture, examine currently supported knowledge-base choices. The key exam question is whether you need an intent-and-slot conversational workflow.

scenes.title: Amazon Personalize
scenes.narration: Amazon Personalize helps a product suggest relevant items using user interaction records and optional metadata. A retailer might collect views, purchases and cart events, then learn which products users tend to engage with. A model trained only on old events can miss changing interests, so applications may ingest new interaction events and periodically refresh their approach. Recommendations can appear on websites, mobile apps, notifications or emails. This is different from a model composing a natural language recommendation explanation; Personalize focuses on ranking or selecting relevant items or actions. Businesses must protect user data, measure usefulness and be careful about feedback loops that repeatedly promote a small set of already popular products. Evaluate recommendation quality against meaningful outcomes while respecting consent and data retention requirements.

scenes.title: Amazon Personalize – Recipes
scenes.narration: The word recipe in Amazon Personalize refers to a supported algorithmic approach for a particular recommendation task. User-Personalization-v2 suggests items for a user, while Personalized-Ranking-v2 orders a supplied list. Similar-Items looks for related products. Trending-Now and Popularity-Count address popularity in different ways. Next-Best-Action recommends an action, while Item-Affinity can support segmentation rather than a simple single-user recommendation response. This is why it is wrong to assume that every recipe uses the same API or serving workflow. Some recipes support online campaigns while others use action recommendations or batch segment jobs. Start with the question the business needs answered, then check required datasets and supported operations. If the company already knows which items are eligible and only wants to reorder them, personalized ranking is more suitable than generating an unconstrained catalog.
